To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) fire acts on breeding bird communities mainly by altering the total abundance patterns; (ii) the effects of fire are more evident at guild than at community level; and (iii) the effects of forest fire on breeding birds depend on the species’ ecological guild.

fire acted on breeding birds by decreasing the abundance of forest species and increasing the abundance of edge/open habitat species, and by inducing a turnover in species composition between pinewoods.

(1) fire affected the abundance of the breeding bird community; (2) the species richness of the breeding bird communities was not affected by fire; (3) the edge and open-habitat species increased, whereas the forest species decreased in burnt pinewoods; (4) the edge and forest species showed the highest and lowest species turnover, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of a catastrophic fire event on the breeding bird community, guilds and selected species, in burnt and control residual pinewoods of central Italy.

the effects of fire on the bird communities of burnt residual pinewoods and their comparison with unburnt residual ones, in order to assess whether fire can be considered as a disturbance factor, or a natural process.
the effects of a fire catastrophe on breeding birds in a Mediterranean residual pinewood.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fire acts as a disturbance on breeding bird communities in pinewoods, and that the effects are mainly on species richness and abundance.
fire acts on bird communities by altering the abundance and richness of the species, and by modifying the species composition.

fire is a disturbance factor that affects bird community and guild composition, by changing the abundance and richness of the various species, and that this effect depends on the intensity of the fire and on the time elapsed from the burning event.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the catastrophic fire event in 2000, which burned the whole pinewood of Castelfusano, had a strong negative impact on breeding birds in terms of total abundance.
, in a Mediterranean pinewood, the effects of fire on birds are mainly related to the loss of forest habitat, which is the main factor affecting bird species and guilds.
the fire effects on bird communities are mainly related to habitat structure, and that the edge and open-habitat species are more resilient to fire disturbance than the forest species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fire, by changing habitat conditions, induces a strong shift in species composition, which is especially pronounced in burnt pinewoods.

fire, in a Mediterranean context, can be a useful tool in managing pinewoods for biodiversity conservation, provided that the fire is applied in a controlled and limited way, in order to maintain a mosaic of different habitat structures and to preserve the forest component of the landscape.
, after a fire event, the bird species which are most likely to be affected are the forest ones.
